name: Nuclear plant safety
summary: Zaporizhzhia relies on a single power line as Russian strikes hit Ukraine's grid
state: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has relied on a single off-site line since repairs agreed under an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire (Arms Control Association). Russian strikes continued to hit Ukraine's energy system into 5 Nov (Forbes). No damage to safety systems or radiological release has been reported.
for_you: No public health action is advised; follow IAEA and national regulator updates.
rubric_hit: Plant on minimal off-site power amid grid strikes = Watch

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Russia, Ukraine agree to repairs at Zaporizhzhia
Forbes — Ukraine braces for winter amid Russian attacks on its energy sector

why: Fighting near nuclear power plants risks a radiological release; the IAEA reports on Zaporizhzhia and other plants in or near war zones.
drivers: Off-site power losses, strikes near plants, staffing, cooling water, military occupation.

rubric.alert: Damage to safety-critical systems, an INES level 2 or higher event, or a radiological release.
rubric.watch: A plant loses all off-site power, strikes land near a plant, or the IAEA reports a deteriorating safety situation.
rubric.normal: No new IAEA safety concerns at plants in or near conflict zones.
